correctness.rationale: The 2022 published record-subset bijection parametrizes every source of a fixed one-pass bubble-sort output ending in its maximum. Swapping two adjacent entries changes the source record set by at most one value. If the toggled selected record has intervening source-output letters since the preceding selected record, toggling yields factors μWν versus νWμ and is not a single adjacent swap; otherwise W is empty and it is one swap. Consequently bit one always flips, and bit j≥2 flips exactly when original records j−1 and j occupy consecutive positions and bit j−1 is zero. Splitting at permanent frozen coordinates gives the stated Cartesian product and the frozen-first-bit H_L component decomposition. Counting consecutive prefinal record positions gives C_n. The only numerical steps are diagnostic: full actual-fiber adjacency/BFS checks through n=8 and exact count arithmetic through n=250 using the embedded verify.py.

originality.rationale: The nearest full primary source supplies the vertex parametrization and a different sorting-tree adjacency under complete passes, not the induced equal-output one-adjacent-swap graph. The new assertion is a sharp all-output graph classification, record-gap-dependent components, exact sizes and a connected-output census; none is a special case of a documented stronger fiber-connectivity theorem in the inspected sources. Other related full bubble-sort network connectivity results concern the entire Cayley graph and cannot imply connectivity of arbitrary induced subsets. General facilitated-cube factors and the source bijection themselves are not claimed novel. Priority remains qualified by unindexed equivalents.

value.rationale: Reachability under an output-preserving elementary adjacent swap is natural in sorting/reconfiguration and cannot be inferred from the number of preimages. The theorem completely characterizes those components and their sizes for every possible output and proves a sharp decay e/(n−1) for connected exact-output fibers. The exact edge formula and constructive connectedness test are useful in optimal local enumeration and random walks confined to a sorting-pass fiber. This is a motivated, parameter-uniform structural result rather than an arbitrary computed invariant.
